status: config checked against the docs, not run in our build (these hosts cannot run on Modal)

files.hosts/claude_desktop_config.json: Claude Desktop: local stdio servers only. macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json, Windows %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json; top-level mcpServers {name: {command, args, env}}. Remote servers (our HTTP variant, the GitHub remote server) are added in Settings > Connectors > Add custom connector (a URL), not in this file.
files.hosts/vscode_mcp.json: VS Code: .vscode/mcp.json (workspace) or the user profile; top-level 'servers' (required), 'inputs' (optional), 'sandbox' (optional). stdio: type, command, args, cwd, env, envFile. http/sse: type, url, headers, oauth. Secrets via inputs[] {type: promptString, id, description, password: true} referenced as ${input:id}; VS Code prompts once and stores it securely. The portable .mcp.json uses 'mcpServers' and does not support ${input:...}.
files.hosts/cursor_mcp.json: Cursor: .cursor/mcp.json (project) or ~/.cursor/mcp.json (global); top-level mcpServers. stdio: type 'stdio', command, args, env, envFile. Remote: url, headers, auth (no type in the docs' remote examples). Secrets via ${env:NAME} interpolation (also ${userHome}, ${workspaceFolder}).

sources.title: Add MCP servers in VS Code
GitHub MCP Server README (remote URL https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/, VS Code 1.101+ for remote MCP and OAuth)

notes: Every snippet parses as JSON (checked with python json.load).
No literal token anywhere: VS Code uses ${input:github_pat} (or OAuth with the url-only 'github' entry), Cursor uses ${env:GITHUB_PAT}.
Our server must be importable by the host's python: pip install the course package first (bahi-erp from the course repo).
The stdio command and the HTTP variant were run for real on Modal by MCP Inspector (logs/inspector_run.json); the host apps themselves were not.
